note: No rule of the State Bank of Vietnam or NAPAS fixing an account number's length was read (sbv.gov.vn answered 403). BIDV, the largest bank, announced (its notices read 2026-10-30) that from 15 January 2025 transfers to and from BIDV accounts use only the shortened numbers its new core banking system gives, 3 to 8 or 10 digits long, in place of the old 14 digits, and that from 15 July 2025 transfers to or from 14-digit accounts are discontinued. So the number is written as 3 to 10 digits; the form can't leave out 9, which BIDV doesn't give, and a new account is drawn at the most, 10. Other banks' lengths weren't read from their own pages, and a longer number at another bank would be refused: a reading the lead should check. The transfer names the receiving bank beside the number; no bank code sits in it. No check digit is published.

sources.title: BIDV (Joint Stock Commercial Bank for Investment and Development of Vietnam), Notification on converting account numbers under the new core banking system
sources.said: BIDV respectfully announces that from January 15, 2025, customers who use accounts at BIDV as transfer accounts, or transfer money to beneficiary accounts at BIDV, should only use accounts that have been shortened (3-8 and 10 digits long instead of 14 digits.

sources.title: BIDV, BIDV Stops Using 14-Digit Account Numbers
sources.said: the mandatory use to shortened account numbers (3–8 or 10 digits) in place of 14-digit accounts ... from 15 July 2025, money transfers to or from 14-digit accounts will be discontinued
